short_title: What happens if you drink too much water? 💧 #shorts
short_description:
Your kidneys have a speed limit. Healthy kidneys can get rid of roughly 0.8 to 1 liter of water an hour (about a quart). Drink a lot more than that in a short time, and the extra water dilutes the sodium in your blood. This is called hyponatremia, or water intoxication: water moves into your cells and they swell, including in the brain, which can cause headache, nausea and confusion. Severe cases are rare but can be life-threatening, for example during water-drinking contests or very long endurance races.

The simple rule: drink when you're thirsty, sip, don't chug. If you have a medical condition, ask your doctor.
